title: Places Where People Gather
bigQuestion: What do people do in places of worship, and how can we be a good guest?

story.title: Five Doors on One Street
story.kicker: Theo walks down one Chicago street and sees five special doors.
paragraphs: Theo walks with his grandpa down a long Chicago street. "Look," says Grandpa. "Five doors. Each opens on a special day."
On Friday, people go into a mosque. Some take off their shoes. Friday evening, families walk to a synagogue. On Saturday, they read from a big scroll.
On Sunday, bells ring at a church. People sing inside. Down the block is a Hindu temple with bright colors. Next is a gurdwara. People cover their heads and share a free meal.
"Do we go in one?" Theo asks. "Not every family does," says Grandpa. "Some do, and some do not. But we can learn about all of them."
story.think: What did Theo see at each door? Which place would you like to learn about?

lessons.title: A Place to Gather
lessons.mainIdea: A place of worship is where a group meets to pray, sing, read and learn.
reading: Worship means to pray, sing or show love to God or to what is holy. Many religions have a special building for it.
People gather there. They pray. They sing. They read from holy books. They learn and eat together. Not every family goes to one. That is okay.

words.d: to pray, sing or show love to God or to what is holy
very special and set apart, for people of a religion

look.title: What Do You Hear?
look.text: Close your eyes. You hear people singing together. Someone reads out loud. Then it is quiet while people pray. After, you smell food and hear friends talk.
look.prompt: What are the people doing in this place?

check.q: What is a place of worship?
choices: A place where a group meets to pray and learn
check.why: People gather there to pray, sing and learn.

check.q: Does every family go to a place of worship?
check.why: Not every family goes. That is okay.

check.q: What does worship mean?
choices: To pray, sing or show love to God or what is holy
check.why: Worship means to pray, sing or show love to God or what is holy.

lessons.title: Holy Days to Gather
lessons.mainIdea: Many groups gather on a special day each week.
reading: Many Muslims gather at a mosque at midday on Friday. They pray together. Then they may visit with friends.
The Jewish Sabbath, Shabbat, starts Friday at sunset. It ends Saturday night. Many Jewish families go to a synagogue. Many Christians go to church on Sunday.

words.d: a day of rest; for Jewish families, from Friday sunset to Saturday night

look.title: Weekly Gathering Days
rows: Jewish families at a synagogue: Saturday
look.cite: Common weekly practice; some groups gather on other days too
look.prompt: Which group gathers last in the week?

check.q: When do many Muslims gather to pray together?
check.why: Many Muslims pray together at a mosque on Friday.

check.q: When does Shabbat start?
check.why: Shabbat starts Friday at sunset.

check.q: Many Christians go to church on which day?
check.why: Many Christians go to church on Sunday.

lessons.title: Church and Synagogue
lessons.mainIdea: Christians gather in churches; Jewish people gather in synagogues.
reading: A church is where Christians worship. Many have a cross. Some have tall towers and bells. Inside, people sing, pray and read from the Bible.
A synagogue is where Jewish people worship. Inside is a cabinet called the ark. It holds the Torah scroll. The Torah is the first five books of the Hebrew Bible.

words.d: a building where Jewish people worship and learn
the first five books of the Hebrew Bible, written on a scroll

look.title: Glad to Go
look.text: I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the LORD.
look.cite: The Bible, Psalm 122:1, King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: This song is in both the Jewish and Christian Bible. How does the singer feel about going?

check.q: What is kept in the ark in a synagogue?
check.why: The ark holds the Torah scroll.

check.q: Where do Christians worship?
check.why: Christians worship in a church.

check.q: What is the Torah?
choices: The first five books of the Hebrew Bible
check.why: The Torah is the first five books of the Hebrew Bible.

lessons.title: The Mosque
lessons.mainIdea: Muslims pray in a mosque, often on soft rugs, facing toward Mecca.
reading: A mosque is where Muslims pray. Many have a round dome. Some have a tall tower called a minaret.
People take off their shoes. They wash before they pray. They stand in rows on soft rugs. They all face toward Mecca, a holy city in Saudi Arabia.

words.d: a holy city for Muslims; they face toward it to pray

look.title: Rows on the Rug
look.text: Look inside. There are no chairs. A big soft rug covers the floor. People stand in straight rows, side by side. Shoes wait in a rack by the door.
look.prompt: Why do you think the shoes are by the door?

check.q: What do people do with their shoes in a mosque?
check.why: People take off their shoes in a mosque.

check.q: Which way do Muslims face to pray?
check.why: Muslims face toward Mecca to pray.

check.q: What is a minaret?
choices: A tall tower on some mosques
check.why: A minaret is a tall tower on some mosques.

lessons.title: A Hindu Temple
lessons.mainIdea: Hindus visit a temple to pray and see images of the gods.
reading: A Hindu temple is often bright and full of carvings. People take off their shoes. Some ring a bell as they come in.
Inside are images of gods and goddesses. Hindus bring gifts like flowers, fruit and light. They pray and sing. Many Hindus pray at home too.

words.d: a building where some groups, like Hindus, worship

look.title: Gifts at the Temple
look.text: A girl holds a plate. On it are orange flowers, a banana and a tiny flame. She rings a bell. Then she steps up to pray.
look.prompt: What gifts does she bring? What might they show?

check.q: What might Hindus bring to a temple?
check.why: Hindus bring gifts like flowers and fruit.

check.q: Where do Hindus worship?
choices: At a temple and at home
check.why: Hindus pray at temples and at home.

check.q: What might someone ring when they come into a Hindu temple?
check.why: Some ring a bell as they come in.

lessons.title: The Gurdwara
lessons.mainIdea: Sikhs gather at a gurdwara, where anyone can share a free meal.
reading: A gurdwara is where Sikhs worship. Their holy book is the Guru Granth Sahib. People sing its hymns.
Everyone covers their head and takes off their shoes. After prayer comes langar. Langar is a free meal. Everyone sits together and eats. Anyone may come, of any faith.

words.d: a free meal at a gurdwara, shared with anyone who comes

look.title: Everyone at One Meal
look.text: Look at the long hall. People sit side by side on the floor. Helpers bring bowls of lentils and warm bread. No one pays. A grandma, a student and a visitor eat together.
look.prompt: What does this meal show about Sikh ideas of sharing?

check.q: What is langar?
choices: A free meal shared with anyone
check.why: Langar is a free meal at a gurdwara.

check.q: What is the Sikh holy book?
check.why: Sikhs read the Guru Granth Sahib.

check.q: Who can eat langar?
check.why: Anyone may come to langar.

lessons.title: Guest Manners
lessons.mainIdea: A good guest uses a quiet voice and follows the rules of the place.
reading: You might visit a place of worship with a friend. Be a good guest! Use a quiet voice. Watch what others do.
Some places ask you to take off your shoes. Some ask you to cover your head. If you are not sure, ask kindly. You can watch without joining in.

words.d: a visitor to someone's home or place

look.title: Visiting with a Friend
look.text: Ava visits a gurdwara with her friend Harpreet. She sees a basket of head scarves by the door. People are taking off their shoes. It is quiet inside.
look.prompt: What should Ava do? How can she find out?

check.q: What voice should a guest use?
check.why: A good guest uses a quiet voice.

check.q: You are not sure what to do. What helps?
check.why: Asking kindly helps.

check.q: At a gurdwara, what do guests do?
check.why: Everyone covers their head at a gurdwara.

lessons.title: A Walk in Chicago
lessons.mainIdea: Chicago has many kinds of places of worship, close together.
reading: Chicago has people from all over the world. So it has many places of worship. You can find churches, synagogues, mosques, temples and gurdwaras.
Near Chicago, in Wilmette, is the Baha'i House of Worship. It is white and has nine sides. People of all faiths may visit it.

words.d: a person who lives near you

look.title: Our Street Walk
look.text: Pretend to walk one block. First, a church with a bell. Next, a synagogue with a star on the door. Then a mosque with a dome. Last, a gurdwara with a tall flag.
look.prompt: Which place did you pass first? Which one would you ask about?

check.q: Why does Chicago have many places of worship?
choices: People came from all over the world
It is a very small town
check.why: People from all over the world live in Chicago.

check.q: What is in Wilmette, near Chicago?
check.why: The Baha'i House of Worship is in Wilmette.

check.q: How many sides does the Baha'i House of Worship have?
check.why: It has nine sides.

review.q: What holy book is kept in a synagogue's ark?
review.why: The ark holds the Torah scroll.

choices: A free meal at a gurdwara
review.why: Langar is a free meal at a gurdwara.

review.q: What should a good guest do if not sure?
Many Christians go to church on which day?
review.why: Many Christians go to church on Sunday.

review.q: Where might you take off your shoes?
choices: In a mosque or a Hindu temple
review.why: Shoes come off in a mosque, a Hindu temple and a gurdwara.
